Inside a gate

The same chip at four depths: the SystemVerilog it is written in, the 5,991 standard cells synthesis turns it into, the transistors inside each cell, and how those transistors are drawn in silicon.

Everything below comes from real files: the RTL in src/, a Yosys 0.33 synthesis to the SkyWater sky130 high-density cell library (52,984.6 µm², 61,160 transistors counted from the SkyWater SPICE netlists), and the SkyWater layouts of the 72 cell types it uses. docs/tools/views_build.py builds it; nothing on this page is drawn by hand.

How to use it

Every highlighted thing is a viewing point: choose it and every view that can show it follows. Choose a module on the left, then a register: its RTL lines light up and the gates that compute its next value are drawn. Choose a gate to open its transistors and layout. Flip the inputs and watch which transistors conduct. Below, the state machines are a common language between the views: a state is a case arm in the RTL, one flip-flop in the gates, and a circle in the diagram. The address bar keeps your place, so a view can be linked.

How each view is checked

  • Layout is the transistors. KLayout's netlist extractor rebuilds the circuit from each cell's polygons and compares it with the SkyWater SPICE netlist, transistor by transistor (type, width, length, connections): python3 docs/tools/views_lvs.py. A second, independent geometric check measures every channel: python3 test/views/mini_lvs.py.
  • The transistors are the gate. A switch-level simulation of each cell's transistors, for every input combination, must give the liberty Boolean function; flip-flops must load D on a rising clock and hold otherwise: python3 docs/tools/views_switch.py. The transistor view on this page uses the same rules, and test/views/page_test.js checks the two agree on every cell.
  • The gates are the RTL. The gate netlist and the RTL run side by side on the same programs, with random pin activity, and every output pin is compared on every clock: make -C test views.
  • The diagrams are what the chip does. The same runs log both state machines every clock; each step must be an arrow of the diagram, and the gate flip-flops must hold the one-hot code synthesis chose: python3 test/views/fsm_check.py.
  • The instruction table is real machine code. Every row is assembled, and each opcode is checked against the value the core decodes: python3 docs/tools/views_isa.py --check.

illustrative The FinFET drawing in the layout view is a comparison sketch. Every transistor in this chip is a planar MOSFET; SkyWater 130 nm has no FinFETs.

Tiqora is a RISC-V microcontroller for a Tiny Tapeout 3x2 tile on SkyWater sky130. Nothing on these pages has run on real silicon or a real FPGA board; every number says how it was obtained.

Built by docs/tools/build_site.py from the RTL's own recordings and measurements. Maintained by @Normansrule. Source, tests and issues: github.com/Normansrule/tiqora-skywater130. Its sibling: Tiqora-Serial, the same timing unit without a processor.
